gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold defect is that a global dG-star seminorm is applied to a local interpolant defined only on K, leaving other elements and interior faces uncontrolled or undefined. ISSUE-003 instead diagnoses a separate regularity and continuity failure for the nodal interpolant of p_{tt} in the d=2, q=1 case. Its regularity repair does not recognize the local-versus-global domain mismatch or the missing global dG estimate.

The gold concern is that Picard–Lindelöf and the claimed C2/C1 solution regularity are unsupported for merely L2-in-time acoustic and concentration sources, requiring time-continuity of the sources. ISSUE-002 instead concerns the definition of the continuation time, propagation of a pressure closeness bound over every prior time, and membership in the nondegenerate set. It does not diagnose the missing temporal regularity of the forcing data.

Both entries identify the omitted approximation requirement on the discrete initial concentration and the resulting loss of the initial error term when integrating the concentration energy inequality. They also give the same substantive repair: impose an O(h^q) initial approximation or choose the interpolant, and retain the initial energy term.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The concentration convergence estimate assumes an O(h^q) approximation of the initial discrete concentration, but the theorem permits arbitrary discrete initial data and the proof drops the resulting initial energy term.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem allows arbitrary discrete initial concentration data even though the stated rate requires the initial L2 error to be O(h^q).
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly states that no condition is imposed on u^h_0 and that the claimed estimate is false for general discrete initial concentration data.

component_coverage.gold_component: The integrated energy argument must retain and control the initial error term ||I_h u_0-u^h_0||^2.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 identifies the initial term produced by integration, explains that the proof silently drops it, and requires including it and imposing a suitable initial approximation condition.
